one_line: Anthropic and Meta ship new models, Google adds TPUs, and Nvidia faces a board probe over its CEO.

themes.title: New model releases from Anthropic and Meta
themes.text: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, priced at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, with outputs up to 30% faster than the 5.1 versions; researcher Ethan Mollick used Fable 5.2 to direct 25,000 agents in building over 450 code-generated 3D worlds. Meta's Superintelligence Lab also released Muse Ember, its lightest model at $0.10 per million input tokens, aimed at repetitive agent tasks such as tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, and long document parsing.

themes.title: Compute buildout accelerates
themes.text: Google announced TPU 8tx for confidential inference paired with AMD CPUs and TPU 8i Max for long-context tasks, both scheduled for 2027, alongside native PyTorch support and an open-source XLA Serving Engine. On the compute side, SpaceX plans a $24 billion gas power plant and super-compute facility in Starbase, Texas; ByteDance is weighing a larger second phase of its 300-megawatt data center in Ceará, Brazil; and former U.S. DOE staffers launched modular data center firm Mavria, raising $130 million at a $1 billion valuation.

themes.title: Nvidia board probes CEO over spy allegations
themes.text: Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang admitted an extramarital affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials allege is a Chinese spy; shares fell over 4% and Huang withdrew from the ElevenLabs Summit and other speaking engagements. Separately, a Commerce Department probe of Megaspeed for diverting Nvidia AI chips to China was transferred to the Justice Department after Nvidia contacted the agency.

themes.title: Regulators and safety concerns mount
themes.text: The European Commission is set to consider the Digital Fairness Act, which would require companies to let adults disable addictive features and target AI systems that simulate relationships, addressing consumer harm estimated at €7.9 billion annually. In the U.S., Trump claimed the DOJ threatened a top AI executive with arrest over alleged misconduct, without naming the person or company. Fireworks disclosed a cyberattack exposing customer datasets, incomplete model weights, and billing information, and Tencent's chief AI scientist warned that AI models will soon master biology and present safety risks.
